full_judgment:
5. Md Mostafizur Rahman, the petitioner No. 3, also sat for the Special Superior Service, Examination, 1973 (batch II) as non-freedom fighters. After qualifying in the said examination and on successful completion of training was posted as Circle Officer (Development) in Grade VI in pursuance of the notification dated 20-5-1977. Md Abu Baker, the petitioner No. 4, also passed the Superior Service Examination held in 1973 as a non Freedom Fighter. He also received various trainings in NIPA and BARD like the other two petitioners. The petitioner Nos. 3 and 4, on the recommendations of the Public Service Commission, were promoted as Assistant Commissioners on Probation of the BCS (Admin) Cadre in pursuance of the Memo dated 15-1-1984, issued by the Ministry of Establishment, Government of Bangladesh (Annexure Z-2). It appears that the services of the petitioner Nos. 3 and 4 were confirmed as Assistant Commissioners in Grade V. However, in pursuance of a departmental proceeding by an Order dated 4-7-1993, published in Bangladesh Gazette on 22-7-1993, the petitioner No. 3, was reduced to a lower time scale for three years by way of punishment (Annexure J-5). In the meantime, the service of Md Abu Bakkar the petitioner No. 4, was confirmed in the post of Assistant Commissioner. He also passed the senior scale examination and was promoted to the post of Senior Assistant Commissioner and in due course got the selection grade (9,500-12,100). The grievance of the petitioner Nos. 3 and 4 is that although they were promoted to the post of Assistant Commissioner by notification dated 15-14984, they were not given their due promotion along with their colleagues and they were victims of discrimination in violation of their fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution. These variously aggrieved petitioners made representations to the Government but failed to get any response, as such, they were constrained to issue a notice demanding justice through their learned Advocate on 2-12-2001 (Annexure K) but still without any response from the respondents as such obtained the present Rule against Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Establishment and two others to show cause as to why the petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 should not be encadred in the Bangladesh Civil Service (Admn: Admn) Cadre and why the petitioner Nos. 1 to 4 should not be declared to have been appointed to Class I posts from 1977 in the upgraded posts of Circle Officer in Grade V under the Services Re-organization Scheme and why a direction should not be issued to treat the petitioner Nos. 1 to 4 as belonging to 1972 batch with all benefits of seniority and promotion under the provisions of law. 

 8. Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate a In behalf of the petitioners, took us through the petition and also the various papers ting from 1972 giving a very grim background of the entire episode of the petitioners in this writ petition and submits that the petitioners were all bright young men sought to get in the service of the new Republic of Bangladesh in 1972 and the aspirants successfully appeared in the Special Superior Services Examination held for non-freedom fighters in pursuance of the public notices published on 6-7-1972, that although all of them were successful in the examination and also received various trainings from time to time but had to wait for the next more than 5 years for their appointment in Grade V service for which they appeared in 1972 but after a long delay were ultimately placed in the Grade VI in the posts of Circle Officer along with many other such candidates. Since, the learned Advocate submits, they were at the end of their patience after awaiting for more than 5 years and by that time they also crossed their age limit, as such, they had no other alternative but to accept such postings as was made available to them by the Government but still hoped that someday they would be properly placed in Grade V services, that their perseverance was rewarded when ultimately the petitioners No. 1 and 2 were posted as Assistant Commissioners by a notification dated 6-9-1983 although in their earlier scale of pay at Grade VI. The learned Advocate further submits that they rendered their services as Assistant Commissioners and Deputy Magistrates to the satisfaction of their superiors but to their dismay they were not formally placed in Grade V for no fault of the petitioners, as such, they made representations to the authorities but without any response. The learned Advocate submits that the facts remain that the petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 rendered their services as Assistant Commissioners in various places of postings to the entire satisfaction of the Superior Officers as such there was no reason to confirm them in Grade V with effect, at least from their postings in 1983, if not from 1977. 

 9. The learned Advocate further submits that the facts remain that the petitioner No. 1 rendered his service as Assistant Commissioner successfully to the satisfaction of his different superior officers such as Deputy Commissioners, Divisional Commissioners who recommended for his regularisation in the said post but, on the contrary, he was ultimately reverted back after rendering the service for more than 7 years as an Assistant Commissioner, for reasons not known to him. Similarly, the petitioner No. 2 also rendered his services till 2001 for the last more than 17 years and suddenly he was reverted to the post of Administrative Officer, which is nothing more than the post of a glorified clerk, to his dismay. Similarly the petitioner No. 3 also served as an Assistant Commissioner with Magisterial powers but after serving successfully in the said post for a very long period of time on the verge of retirement but was not promoted to any higher posts although he was posted on a regular basis as an Assistant Commissioner by notification dated 15-1-1984. Similar is the case with the petitioner No. 4 who after a long service of nearly 20 years had already gone for a leave preparatory to retirement without any promotion in his long and unblemished career. Under this painful circumstances, the learned Advocate submits that the petitioners when all of them are on the verge of retirement they were constrained to file this writ petition under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh as their fundamental rights were violated in not placing them in their proper posts even after rendering a very long and faithful service in the Republic. 

 12. It will rather be illogical to post officers of one Grade to a higher Grade unless the Government decides so as a policy decision. In the instant case, as many as 76 Circle Officers (Development) including the petitioners Nos. 1 to 3, by a notification dated 6-9-1983 (Annexure E) were posted in different Upazilas against the vacancy of Assistant Commissioners. On such appointment, the petitioners rendered their services in version:- capacities in the rank and status of Assistant Commissioners and also worked as Deputy Magistrates and Deputy Collectors with enhancement of Magisterial powers from Third Class to even First Class. The petitioner Nos. 1 and 2, after working for so many years as such Assistant Commissioners suddenly were reverted back to Grade VI postings without any rhyme or reason. If they were not to be confirmed in Grade V then the Government in the first place, ought not to have posted them as such Assistant Commissioners but after having done so and received their such service in the said post of the Assistant Commissioners, to the satisfaction of their Superior Officers, it is very unfair on the part of the Government to revert them back in Grade VI for no fault of the petitioners.
